prompt: gnulib pthread_rwlock_trywrlock error code already owned write lock
answer:
On glibc/Linux, `pthread_rwlock_trywrlock()` returns `EBUSY` when the lock is already held for writing—including when it is held by the calling thread. glibc’s implementation unconditionally returns `EBUSY` when acquisition fails.

`EDEADLK` applies to `pthread_rwlock_wrlock()`, not to the POSIX `pthread_rwlock_trywrlock()` error list. Therefore, gnulib should treat `EBUSY` as “already locked,” but cannot use it alone to determine whether the current thread owns the write lock. Explicit ownership tracking is required if that distinction matters.

Sources: [glibc implementation](https://codebrowser.dev/glibc/glibc/nptl/pthread_rwlock_trywrlock.c.html), [POSIX specification](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/pthread_rwlock_wrlock.html).
